Arch bridge

Arch bridge
TypeBridge
MaterialStone, steel
SpanShort to medium

An arch bridge is a bridge with abutments at each end shaped as a curved arch. Arch bridges work by transferring the weight of the structure to the supports.

Contents
  1. History
  2. Construction
  3. Uses

History

The earliest bridges were simple logs laid across narrow streams. Roman engineers perfected the stone arch, and many of their spans still carry traffic.

Iron and later steel allowed builders to cross far wider rivers than before. A well designed truss spreads the load through many small triangles. Wind can be as dangerous to a long bridge as the weight of the traffic.

Uses

Water that is just below boiling extracts the pleasant flavours without bitterness. Freshly roasted beans are usually best within a few weeks. Many cafes now list the farm or cooperative that grew their beans.

Cold brew is steeped for many hours and tastes smooth and sweet. Coffee plants grow best on high slopes with mild temperatures and steady rain. After harvest, the ripe cherries are dried or washed to remove the fruit. Roasting changes the colour, aroma and flavour of the green beans.
